access: Recommended lesson completed in the signed-in Chrome session on the free tier.
knowledge_learned: Start with an integer greater than 1. Split each composite node into two smaller positive factors whose product equals that node. Stop at prime leaves. A split using 1 and the parent itself does not reduce the parent.

Multiplying all the leaves recovers the starting number. The fundamental theorem of arithmetic guarantees that every valid tree for the same number has the same prime factors with the same multiplicities, regardless of branching or order.
Repeated prime leaves constrain missing branch values. Two equal prime leaves give a prime square at their parent, and three equal prime leaves give a prime cube at the root.
mechanics_observed: The worked example reveals one branch at a time and marks composite nodes and prime leaves with different shapes.
Learners count valid trees by checking branch products and spotting early stops or invalid splits.
Later questions hide branch values, ask learners to match a tree shape to a number, and compare differently shaped trees with the same number of leaves.
Multiple-choice questions use explicit Check, immediate feedback, optional Why explanations, a progress bar, and Finish.
